questions: Should the function also search the transpose of the DataFrame as the prompt mentions 'or its transpose', or is that a misinterpretation and only the original DataFrame should be searched?
When sample_size is provided but random_seed is None, should the random sampling be deterministic (e.g., using a default seed) or non-deterministic (system time)?
If sample_size is greater than or equal to the number of positions, should the function return all positions (as the reference does) or should it still sample with replacement up to sample_size?
When sampling, should positions be selected with or without replacement? The reference uses randint repeatedly which allows duplicates, but is that intended?

The prompt says 'record its frequency distribution' but the output doesn't include any distribution; should the function compute and return a frequency distribution (e.g., counts per column/row) or is that just descriptive?
Are the dictionary keys required to be integers starting from 1, or can they be any hashable type? The clarification says values are lists, but keys are ambiguous.

If a value list is shorter than others, should missing values be filled (e.g., with NaN) or should the DataFrame have columns of unequal length? The reference uses pd.DataFrame directly which pads with NaN.

Should the function handle the case where the item appears multiple times in a single cell (if values are nested lists)? The clarification says values are lists, but not whether they can contain the item in sublists.
